rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes high-pressure spark plasma sintering (SPS) as a processing modification for W–Cu composites, while the hidden target uses liquid-metal dealloying (LMD) in molten Cu to create a RHEA–Cu composite. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (sintering vs. dealloying).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions sintering under high pressure and rapid heating, and testing under high heat flux and irradiation. The target uses vacuum-sealed LMD at 1200 °C for 96 h, thermal conductivity measurement up to ~800 °C, and 25 keV He+ irradiation. The broad regime of high-temperature processing and irradiation testing is shared, but the specific conditions (LMD vs. SPS, temperature, atmosphere, irradiation energy) are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes enhanced densification and reduced diffusion-driven phase separation/void nucleation via rapid SPS heating. The target's mechanism involves selective dissolution of Ti into Cu, immiscibility-driven retention of W/Ta/V, and formation of a W-rich passivating interlayer. These are different general classes of mechanism (sintering densification vs. selective dealloying and passivation).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts higher, more stable thermal conductivity and reduced phase segregation/voids compared to conventionally sintered joints. The target predicts and achieves substantially increased thermal conductivity (surpassing pure W at high temperature) and reduced He-induced swelling relative to pure W.
